topicTitle: Introduction to Bio-inorganic Chemistry; micro and macro nutrients; importance of metal ions in biological systems (Na, K, Mg, Ca, Fe, Cu, Zn, Ni, Co, Cr)
notes: **Definition:** bio-inorganic chemistry studies the role of metal ions in biological systems.

**Macronutrients:** Na, K, Mg, Ca. Required in larger amounts. Na and K maintain osmotic pressure and nerve impulse transmission. Ca is essential for bones, teeth, and muscle contraction. Mg is central in chlorophyll.
**Micronutrients:** Fe, Cu, Zn, Ni, Co, Cr. Required in trace amounts but vital. Fe in haemoglobin and cytochromes. Zn in carbonic anhydrase and DNA polymerase. Cu in cytochrome c oxidase.
**Ion pumps:** sodium-potassium pump ($Na^+/K^+$-ATPase) moves 3 Na out and 2 K in per ATP, maintaining membrane potential. Sodium-glucose cotransporter uses Na gradient to drive glucose uptake.

**Metal toxicity:** Fe overload causes oxidative damage via Fenton reaction. Arsenic ($As^{3+}$) binds thiol groups in enzymes. Mercury ($Hg^{2+}$) binds to sulfhydryl groups, denaturing proteins. Lead ($Pb^{2+}$) mimics Ca and disrupts neurotransmitter release.
